name: Log Size
definition: The **Log Size** of a family $\mathcal{H}$ is simply the binary logarithm of its cardinality, $$ \log |\mathcal{H}|. $$

monotonic.proof: A subfamily has at most as many distinct concepts as the original class, and the logarithm is increasing.

p_monotonic.proof: A coordinate projection has at most as many distinct concepts as the original class, and the logarithm is increasing.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, being monotonic under both subfamilies and projections is doubly monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection; hence doubly monotonicity implies c-monotonicity.

strict_c_monotonic.proof: If $x$ is effective then both fibres are nonempty and $|\mathcal H|=|\mathcal H_{x=0}|+|\mathcal H_{x=1}|$, so $\log|\mathcal H|$ is strictly larger than the smaller fibre value. Also $\log|\mathcal H|=0$ implies $|\mathcal H|=1$. Thus the definition of strict c-monotonicity holds.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, a doubly monotonic strictly c-monotonic parameter is strictly monotonic.
